subject: Boundary attachment verification & reference diagram handoff
messages:
From: Sofia Ivanova <sofia_ivanova@redwood.ai>
To: Evan Brooks <evan.brooks@edgecloud.io>, Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>, Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-11-02T09:15:00Z
Subject: Boundary attachment verification & reference diagram handoff

Hi Evan / team —

Thanks again for carving out time. Attached are two artifacts we want verified ahead of the control/data-plane dry run next week: 1) boundary-attachment-diagram-v0.3.pdf and 2) deploy-runbook-outline.md. The diagram shows the proposed attachment points: a) a single-mesh transit VPC for control-plane egress to our telemetry collectors, and b) data-plane inference nodes colocated in your on-prem compute cluster behind NAT.

Can you confirm the following items on your side before Thursday so we can finalize the runbook?
- Whether mTLS between Redwood control-plane proxies and your ingress terminators is acceptable (we propose mTLS client certs issued by your internal CA).
- Whether the on-prem egress path allows outbound 443 to the telemetry endpoints listed in the runbook (we include IP ranges in the Drive link).
- If your network team prefers BGP for the transit VPC or static NAT for the initial attach.

If you'd like, we can do a 30-minute walkthrough of the diagram and the proposed canary plan tomorrow afternoon.

Attachments: boundary-attachment-diagram-v0.3.pdf, deploy-runbook-outline.md

Thanks,
Sofia Ivanova
Solutions Engineer — Private Deployments
Redwood Inference
sofia_ivanova@redwood.ai
+1 (415) 555-0142

From: Evan Brooks <evan.brooks@edgecloud.io>
To: Sofia Ivanova <sofia_ivanova@redwood.ai>, Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>, Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.ai>
Cc: partners@acme.com
Date: 2027-11-02T13:05:00Z
Subject: Re: Boundary attachment verification & reference diagram handoff

Sofia — thanks for the artifacts, got them. Quick notes from our infra team after an initial skim:
- mTLS is fine but we ask that Redwood present an X.509 CN that maps to service principal names (we'll provide the mapping table).
- Egress to telemetry is allowed from our firewall but must be pinned to a set of /28s per the rules; can you provide a tightened IP set?
- We prefer BGP for the long-term transit; for the initial attach we can accept static route pairings while we bring up a dedicated BGP session.

I've attached our internal segmentation diagram (edgecloud-onprem-segmentation_v1.drawio) so you can see where the inference nodes will actually live.

Let's do the walkthrough — I have an opening 2027-11-03 16:00 UTC. Works for you?

—Evan
Evan Brooks
Senior NetOps Engineer
EdgeCloud Systems
evan.brooks@edgecloud.io

From: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>
To: Sofia Ivanova <sofia_ivanova@redwood.ai>, Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Evan Brooks <evan.brooks@edgecloud.io>
Date: 2027-11-03T08:42:00Z
Subject: Re: Boundary attachment verification & reference diagram handoff

Thanks Evan — that all sounds reasonable. A few clarifications from the runtime/ops side:
- Control-plane traffic (config, model load, telemetry) will be short-lived TLS flows from our control proxies; we can present service CN mapping as requested. I'll follow up with a surface mapping and cert subject template by EOD.
- For telemetry IPs, we'll publish a minimized /28-aligned set in the Drive link (will attach controlplane-fallback-matrix.xlsx with the split).
- Regarding BGP vs static: agree on starting with static for cutover. We need a documented fallback: if BGP adj goes flappy during the canary, our default is to teardown the BGP session and keep the static pair for the canary window (see row "failover-mode" in the matrix).

Checklist for the walkthrough:
1) Confirm cert CN mapping and rotation cadence.
2) Lock egress IPs and firewall ACL names.
3) Agree canary traffic profile (latency + token throughput) and success criteria for rollback.
4) Confirm what logs EdgeCloud will forward to our audit collector for compliance (we need connection metadata only, not payload).

I'll attach the fallback matrix and copy the Drive link into the runbook page. Jonas

Jonas Weber
Principal Engineer, Inference Runtime
Redwood Inference

From: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.ai>
To: Sofia Ivanova <sofia_ivanova@redwood.ai>, Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>

> > 3) Agree canary traffic profile (latency + token throughput) and success criteria for rollback.
> > 4) Confirm what logs EdgeCloud will forward to our audit collector for compliance (we need connection metadata only, not payload).

All — thanks for the alignment. From an ops + security perspective I'm green on the plan pending two actionable items before the dry run: 1) a short paragraph in the runbook that enumerates the exact rollback steps (who runs them and how to verify), and 2) a verification checklist for the on-prem firewall team that they can tick off during bring-up.

Proposed next steps:
- Sofia: update deploy-runbook-outline.md with a rollback appendix and post to the Drive link.
- Jonas: post final controlplane-fallback-matrix.xlsx into the same folder and add the cert CN template.
- Evan: confirm the /28s you can open for telemetry prior to the canary window.

Once we've got those artifacts I approve the schedule to proceed with the dry run on 2027-11-10 (canary window 12:00–16:00 UTC).

Irene Choi
Director, Cloud Deployments
Redwood Inference
